title: Intervention
novel:
The gang found an old letter in the apartment. It was an [[intervention|intervention]] letter they wrote years ago but never delivered. [[Inspired|inspire]] by the discovery, they decided to hold interventions for each other's [[annoying|annoying]] habits.

Marshall's intervention was about his [[excessive|excessive]] singing. Lily's was about her [[ridiculous|ridiculous]] fake British accent. Ted's was about his [[pretentious|pretentious]] pronunciation of words.

But Barney's intervention was the most [[chaotic|chaotic]]. They [[confronted|confront]] him about his endless [[schemes|scheme]] and crazy behavior. Barney [[reacted|react]] badly. He [[stormed|storm]] out of the apartment and refused to speak to anyone.

The gang felt [[guilty|guilty]]. "Maybe we were too [[harsh|harsh]]," Lily said. They [[gathered|gather]] again and wrote a new letter — this time [[sincere|sincere]] and kind.

Barney returned the next day. He read the letter and [[hesitated|hesitate]]. "You guys really care about me?" he asked, his voice [[cracking|crack]].

"Of course we do," Marshall said.

Barney [[nodded|nod]] slowly. He [[agreed|agree]] to [[tone|tone]] things down — a little. But old habits were [[stubborn|stubborn]], and the gang knew he would never truly change.

That night, they sat together at MacLaren's, laughing about the [[absurd|absurd]] interventions. Friendship, they realized, meant accepting each other — flaws and all.

intervention.en: the act of stepping in to help someone

inspire.en: to give someone a good idea or feeling

excessive.en: too much, more than is reasonable

pretentious.en: trying to seem more important than you are

chaotic.en: in a state of complete confusion

confront.en: to face someone about a problem

react.en: to behave in a particular way in response

guilty.en: feeling bad about something you did

gather.en: to come together in a group

sincere.en: honest and meaning what you say

crack.en: to break, or sound as if breaking

nod.en: to move your head up and down
